title: Exponential-retry accounting gap on streaming requests causing transient silent-allow
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Summary: Intermittent undercounting of streamed token usage occurs when client-side exponential backoff retries are replayed into the streaming ingestion path. Symptoms include silent 'allow' windows for a few seconds followed by a short burst of rejections once accounting catches up. This has led to several customer reports of quota overuse without matching meter increments and one observed billing reconciliation discrepancy.

Why it matters: The bug undermines per-key and per-route accounting guarantees for streaming sessions where retries are expected (e.g., unstable mobile network). It can produce temporary under-billing and permit requests that should be throttled, impacting both revenue and SLO adherence for customers on strict quotas.

Scope: Reproduced in staging and observed in production traces for 3 distinct orgs (low-volume) over the past 30 days. Affects the streaming ingestion path and the async accounting worker that reconciles deduplicated messages. Non-streamed request paths are unaffected.
steps_to_reproduce: Open a streaming generation session against /v1/stream with a small per-key burst quota (e.g., 10 tokens/s).
Simulate flaky network: cause the client to abort the stream and retry with exponential backoff, sending the same client-generated request id header to allow dedupe attempts.
Observe that first few retried fragments are accepted with no immediate meter increment visible in the per-key dashboard; service returns token stream successfully.

After a short delay (1-4s) the async reconciliation worker processes the replayed fragments and meter state updates; at that point the system sometimes issues immediate throttles for subsequent requests.
In a noisy scenario this results in transient silent-allow bursts followed by sharp rejections causing client-visible errors and meter mismatches in billing export.
investigation_findings: Root trigger: race between the streaming fast-path ack and the async dedupe+metering reconciler. Fast-path optimistically returns 'accept' before the atomic debit is durable in the per-key accumulator under certain network retry patterns.

The streaming path uses an in-memory dedupe cache that signals success to the caller pre-commit for latency reasons; however the commit to the durable meter shard is performed asynchronously for retried fragments leading to temporal undercount.
Edge case: exponential backoff spacing causes multiple fragments to be processed after the optimistic accept but before reconciler runs, amplifying the window of silent-allow.
We observed mis-ordered write acknowledgements from the shard leader under load which increases the occurrence rate.
impact_metrics_and_links: Metering dashboard (per-key acceptance vs durable debits): https://console.internal.redwood/dashboards/metering-reconcile
proposed_solution: Primary fix: Ensure streaming fast-path ack is only returned after a durable reservation is written to the meter shard (convert the async reservation + ack to an atomic two-phase commit).

Performance guard: implement a configurable short timeout (50-150ms) for the write; if the durable reservation cannot be confirmed within threshold, return a retryable transient error rather than an optimistic accept.

Backfill/cleanup: run a reconciliation job to attribute any previously uncounted tokens in the last 7 days and surface adjustments to billing pipeline; notify affected customers via billing team draft.
Fallback: add a temporary feature-flag to revert to previous behavior for low-risk orgs while fix lands.
risk_assessment: Low-level code-change in critical path: increases request latency slightly when durable reservation is required. Need to measure P50/P95 impact in staging.
Risk of false throttles if durable write latency spikes beyond threshold; mitigate with conservative timeout and circuit-breaker.
Billing adjustments job requires careful QA to avoid double-charges; coordinate with finance.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge fix behind feature flag and deploy to staging (canary=false).
2) Run load tests targeting stream scenarios; validate P50/P95 request latency increase < 15ms and reconciler gap eliminated.
3) Enable feature flag for 10% of production traffic (non-enterprise orgs) for 48 hours; monitor metering parity and client error rates.
4) Ramp to 50% then 100% with staggered region rollouts; run billing reconciliation job after 100%.
5) Postmortem + communication: notify affected customers and update docs on recommended client retry settings.
testing_plan: Unit tests for streaming reservation state machine and dedupe cache lifecycle.
Integration test that simulates flaky clients with exponential backoff and asserts metering parity (accepts == durable debits) across 10k simulated sessions.
Staging load test with synthetic shard leader write latency variance to validate safety guards.
QA review with finance for billing adjustments job on a 30-day historic slice before running full reconciliation.
implementation_tasks: ENG: refactor streaming fast-path to await durable reservation (Asha).
ENG: add timeout and circuit breaker for durable write (backend infra).
ENG: add monitoring panels and alerts for reconciliation lag (observability team).
ENG: create billing reconciliation job and safe-preview run (billing infra + finance).
PM: customer comms draft and support runbook (Carlos Mendez).
Design: update API docs recommending idempotency headers semantics for streaming retries (Design).
